title: A Backdoor Trigger Is Legible in Fine-Tune Weights
read_level: full (PDF via pdftotext; main text and Limits read closely, appendix tables skimmed)
metadata_mismatch: Corpus abstract is truncated to the first paragraph; full abstract also reports held-out counts and adaptive-attack failures. Otherwise none.
why_wsp: No LLM editor: a hand-designed static statistic reads a fine-tuned checkpoint's weight delta (vs base, standardised against clean fine-tunes) to name a backdoor trigger token without running the suspect; it addresses the weights-to-description question that the WSP blog reported a frontier model failed at.
target: SmolLM2-360M, GPT-2-medium, Qwen2.5-0.5B (reported separately); Pythia-410m in development only

headline_results.quote: it recovers an exact trigger token in 14 of 14 ordinary backdoors on SmolLM2-360M and GPT-2-medium

headline_results.claim: Robust to freeze and camouflage attackers
headline_results.quote: a full freeze of the early block (12 of 14), and a camouflage pass that retrains that block on clean data (10 of 12, including all five rungs of a camouflage ladder)
An attacker that freezes past the scan window and fills the frozen block takes recovery to 0 of 16

headline_results.claim: Statistic-as-penalty attack defeats output criterion at no cost
headline_results.quote: takes recovery to 0 of 2 at every penalty strength, again with attack success at 1.00 and clean accuracy unchanged
0 of 6 clean models flagged against 2 of 6 for the unnormalised statistic, with every backdoor still detected
restoring every scanned weight to its base value leaves attack success at 0.97

cost.quote: under fifteen minutes for a 50k vocabulary on one GPU

baselines_and_controls: Decoy prefixes trained alongside trigger; clean fine-tune null population (five clean models); ablations of per-token standardisation and layer-input basis (Sec IX); calibration repair tested and found worse. No forward-pass trigger-inversion baseline run (stated in Limits).
runs_and_variance: Held-out designs at 2-3 seeds each (Table I: SmolLM2 H0-H3 x two seeds; GPT-2/Qwen G0,G1 x three seeds); "Adaptive results are one or two seeds per cell" (Sec XI).
robustness_of_edits: n/a (detector); robustness of detection tested against freeze, camouflage, norm injection, learning-rate changes, deep freeze + fill, and adaptive gradient penalty.
verification: none formal; rule frozen in writing before held-out designs were built (pre-specification)
limitations_stated: One synthetic task, 12.5% poison rate, frozen embeddings, single payload, nothing above 0.5B parameters; no forward-pass baseline; deep-freeze+fill and statistic-penalty attackers defeat it; reads a correlate, not the mechanism.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (ref [20]; cited as posing and answering negatively the question of reading a fine-tune's training objective)
Dar et al. (vocabulary-space projection of parameters)
notes_for_survey: Non-LLM, closed-form B1 reader positioned against the WSP blog's negative reading result; works on <=0.5B models with full fine-tunes and frozen embeddings. Includes the author's own adaptive attacks that defeat the single-token output criterion.
